clue.text: "Ascertain boffins' choice of poison — and I shall follow suit" (Frenchy)

definitions.text: "Ascertain boffins' choice of poison — and I shall follow suit" (Frenchy)

parts.words: "Ascertain boffins' choice of poison — and I shall follow suit" (Frenchy)
parts.note: a paraphrase of a song title: ascertain = find out, boffins = ... boys, choice of poison = what they will drink, and the singer orders the same

explanation.walkthrough: This looks like it should be a long anagram, but it isn't one. The whole clue rewords the title of the song Frenchy sings in Destry Rides Again (1939). Back-room boys is a British phrase for scientists working out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is a playful paraphrase of the song's title line, with the singer's reply that she will drink the same added on.

clue.text: Cheats on credit — no use to James Bond?

parts.note: to swizzle is British slang for to cheat or swindle
buying on tick is British slang for buying on credit

explanation.surface: A swindler using credit cards is no help to Britain's famous spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' links the two parts and also echoes 'on tick'. Bond likes his martinis shaken, not stirred, so a stirring rod is the one bar tool he has no use for.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar rod for stirring drinks would be useless to a fictional agent who insists his martinis are shaken rather than stirred.

clue.text: School said to be rusty?

indicators.note: said signals that the school's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: Someone is claiming that a school has gone to seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that is rusty has been corroded or eaten away, so the participle works as an adjective here.

clue.text: Yesterday, across the water, Marquis's cockroach's ranking

parts.note: hier is French for yesterday, and France lies across the Channel
archy is the free-verse-writing cockroach in Don Marquis's archy and mehitabel

explanation.surface: A list of French news and a famous cockroach's place in the pecking order.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Marquis was an American humorist; his cockroach archy typed poems by diving head-first onto the keys, so he could never manage capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is a ranking of people or things by status, one level above another.

clue.text: Bad lot, I discovered in the paper

indicators.note: read as dis-covered, the cover is taken off and the letters are jumbled loose

parts.note: used as written for the letter pool

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's misdeeds are exposed in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' rearranges BADLOTI into a word for a popular newspaper; 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a small-format popular newspaper, so it is a paper in the everyday sense.

clue.text: O for a horse painter!

indicators.note: O for a means the letter O takes the place of the letter A

parts.note: a hackney is a breed of high-stepping horse

explanation.surface: An echo of Richard III's cry, 'My kingdom for a horse!'
explanation.walkthrough: The 'O for a ...' pattern and Shakespeare's 'A horse! a horse!' both point to an exclamation. In fact O and A are letters to swap in HACKNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: David Hockney is a leading British painter, known for his swimming-pool pictures.

clue.text: Stone on live railway line

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A stone lies on a live railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a gemstone mineral; emerald and aquamarine are varieties of it.

clue.text: RNAS station that's about to live dangerously

indicators.note: about means the word for that wraps round the other letters

parts.note: yon is an old word for that or those

indicators.note: living dangerously throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A naval air station whose crews are ready to take risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dangerously' turns TO LIVE into EOVILT, and 'about' puts it inside YON. RNAS stands for Royal Naval Air Station.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeovilton in Somerset is the home of a Royal Naval Air Station, the Fleet Air Arm's main base.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
Author Philip in Clarendon to pray wildly for what spa provides

indicators.note: in places the novelist's surname inside the earl's family name

parts.note: Edward Hyde was the first Earl of Clarendon, a 17th-century statesman
Philip Roth was the American novelist
used as written for the letter pool

explanation.surface: An American novelist prays frantically in an English earl's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildly' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container. Clarendon here is a title, not a place or the printing typeface: Edward Hyde was made Earl of Clarendon. 'To' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrotherapy is treatment using water, the kind of cure a spa town offered.

clue.text: Life for a Romany with a lot going for him

definitions.text: Life for a Romany with a lot going for him

parts.note: zing is energy, liveliness or life

indicators.note: going means these letters leave the word before them

parts.note: many is a lot

explanation.surface: A gypsy who has plenty of advantages.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MANY out of ROMANY to leave RO. The whole clue also describes the answer: a Romany man with zing.
explanation.definitionFit: Zingaro is the Italian word for a gypsy man, and the clue describes such a man.

clue.text: Void unchanged — complete reversal unknown

parts.note: read as un changed: the two letters of un with their order switched

indicators.note: complete reversal tells us the word for complete is read backwards

parts.note: to fill something is to complete it
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Something left exactly as it was, a total U-turn, and a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria splits 'unchanged' into 'un' plus 'changed', so the two letters of 'un' are swapped. 'Reversal' turns the word for complete backwards, giving LLIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To void a contract or ruling is to cancel it legally, which is to declare it invalid.

clue.text: Code for "get hiccups"

indicators.note: Araucaria often uses for to mean that the letters sit inside the quoted words

explanation.surface: A secret signal meaning someone has a bout of hiccups.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside gET HICcups.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral code, a set of principles for behaviour.

clue.text: Half a line I make in embroidery lacking time

indicators.note: in puts the I inside the needlework word
lacking says one letter is dropped

parts.note: hemstitch is a decorative embroidery stitch

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have produced an embroidered piece without taking much time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops one T from HEMSTITCH to give HEMSTICH, and 'in' puts I inside; 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemistich is half a line of verse, usually split off by a caesura.

clue.text: Former merchant, preserver of formal religious book, say

parts.note: dry can mean stiff and formal in manner

indicators.note: say signals that the book's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms

explanation.surface: A one-time trader who looked after a stiff old prayer book.
explanation.walkthrough: PSALTER sounds like SALTER. A drysalter dealt in dried and salted foods, dyes and chemicals, so he kept goods from spoiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A drysalter was a historical trader in salted or dried provisions and dyes, a merchant who preserved goods.

clue.text: Heavenly candy left

parts.note: angelica is a plant whose stalks are candied for cake decoration

explanation.surface: Sweets so good that they seem divine, and there are some to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelical is an old variant of angelic, meaning heavenly or like an angel.

clue.text: Hesitation on my account disrupts the internal problem

indicators.note: disrupts means the group breaks into the word the

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Dithering over my accounts upsets an internal investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disrupts' breaks into THE, and 'on' is a link. The surface makes this sound like an inquiry inside an organisation, but the problem is in the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach pain is literally a trouble inside the body, so the definition works in a playful way.

clue.text: Bush product — dog took part in race against time

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
someone who ran took part in a race
T is the standard abbreviation for time; against means placed next to it

explanation.surface: A dog ran a race against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is the small berry that grows on a currant bush.

clue.text: Glance at detective on side of joist, say

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
a joist is a kind of beam; beam also means the side of a ship, which 'on side of' hints at

explanation.surface: A private investigator takes a quick look at the side of a timber beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At', 'on side of' are links, though 'side' also hints at beam as a ship's side (abeam).
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebeam is an old poetic word for a glance, a beam of light from the eye.

clue.text: Cat: plant one for the royal family

indicators.note: plant one for the family says plant and a go in front of the answer to make the name

parts.note: the Plantagenets were an English royal dynasty from 1154 to 1485
used as written
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone plants a feline in the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: PLANT + A + the answer spells PLANTAGENET. Strictly a genet is a cat-like mammal related to the civet rather than a true cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A genet is a slender spotted animal related to the civet and usually loosely described as a wild cat.

clue.text: Dismiss person with money

definitions.meaning: to ... an officer is to dismiss him from the armed forces in disgrace
a bank or shop clerk who handles takings and payments

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means discharge from service, and the noun is a teller who handles the cash.

clue.text: Who's who on the French right that does nothing

parts.note: ID is identity, which says who's who
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A reference book on the French right that achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy loafer is a person who does nothing, so the relative clause stands in for the noun.

clue.text: Overshadow orientals keeping film extracts

indicators.note: keeping means the pair holds the extracts inside it

parts.note: E is east, so two easterners give EE
clips are short extracts from films

explanation.surface: Asian viewers treasure their movie highlights.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to outshine or overshadow it, as the moon blocks the sun.

clue.text: Fear his follower will be Latin American

indicators.note: his follower means the answer comes after the word his

parts.note: Hispanic describes someone of Latin American or Spanish descent

explanation.surface: Someone fears that his successor will come from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: HIS followed by the answer makes HISPANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, so the noun stands in for fear.

clue.text: See 1
Latin American movement prisoner to the state?

parts.note: a con is a convict
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A South American political movement sends a prisoner to the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests politics, but here it is a dance; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Cuban dance in which people move in a long snaking line.

clue.text: Milk (curd with it) they spilt twice so far: here's hoping for the best

definitions.text: twice so far: here's hoping for the best

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters are scattered about

parts.note: used as written
used as written
used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: Someone has knocked over the milk twice and hopes for better luck on the next try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilt' scrambles MILK CURD IT THEY; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying expresses hope that a third attempt will succeed after two failures.
